## T00A — Post-merge dependency graph hardening

**Status:** `DONE` · **Owner:** platform-security · **Milestone:** foundation

**Hard predecessors:** [T00](#t00)
**Platforms:** core, ci
**Connector ports:** None

### Required reading

- [docs/ci/T00_BASELINE.md](../ci/T00_BASELINE.md)
- [docs/roadmap/16-testing-evals-and-quality-gates.md](16-testing-evals-and-quality-gates.md)

Planned targets unless present in the code tree:

```text
tools/verify_ci_lock.py
tools/verify_project_dependency_policy.py
tests/test_ci_lock.py
.github/workflows/ci.yml
docs/ci/T00_BASELINE.md
requirements/README.md
```

### Coding sequence

1. Reproduce all four post-merge Codex findings against the actual current head before changing the validator.
2. Inspect active Requires-Dist edges of every reviewed distribution, validating locked versions and rejecting unsupported extras/direct URLs without fetching dependencies.
3. Reject dynamic dependency/optional-dependency metadata and implicit/missing build-system declarations, or adopt a separately reviewed generated-metadata policy.
4. Capture backend-reported wheel/editable build requirements in a no-download sandbox or explicitly prohibit configurations that can supply unreviewed hooks/requirements. Do not execute arbitrary backend code merely to claim static safety.
5. Add regressions for every bypass plus valid/inactive-marker controls; preserve existing no-deps/hash/duplicate protections.

### Contract and integration handoff

An explicit supported dependency/build configuration and a closed reviewed active graph; document residual trust in the selected backend/toolchain.

### Acceptance evidence

- All four findings have reproducible failing-before/passing-after cases and review disposition.
- Full exact-head Python matrix, compiler/validator/research/wheel checks pass without schema or measurement changes.

### Required failure and regression cases

- Locked child[extra] or direct reference; dynamic dependencies; missing requires/backend; backend setup requirements outside the lock; inactive markers; duplicate metadata.

### Deliverables

- Dependency-policy repairs and regression cases
- Updated post-merge evidence and explicit supported-build policy

### Rollback and compatibility

- Revert scoped policy implementation if defective while keeping affected dependency changes blocked; never allow unsafe installation as fallback.

### Validation and human gates

Validation profiles: [core](#validation-core), [docs](#validation-docs). Planned suites must be implemented and their actual command documented by the owning task; they are not passing tests today.

No task-specific production gate; all repository privacy/security and scope boundaries still apply.

Historical completion evidence: Merged PR #12 (merge bcf5562dde79fd241142fac18abcdde090641b2f); exact head d4647fc70cc06c2fc6633c59be67b1ef5fa83fd3 passed CI run 36273093400 on Python 3.10/3.11/3.12 and roadmap run 36273093435; the Codex code review of that head reported no major issues (issue comment 5850081384). ## T02 — Persistence identity authorization

**Status:** `DONE` · **Owner:** backend · **Milestone:** foundation

**Hard predecessors:** [T01](#t01), [T27](#t27), [T28](#t28)
**Platforms:** backend
**Connector ports:** IdentityProvider

### Required reading

- [docs/roadmap/01-data-architecture.md](01-data-architecture.md)
- [docs/roadmap/09-connectors-and-provider-boundaries.md](09-connectors-and-provider-boundaries.md)
- [docs/connectors/identity.md](../connectors/identity.md)
- [docs/adr/ADR-002-auth-provider.md](../adr/ADR-002-auth-provider.md)
- [docs/adr/ADR-003-postgres-hosting.md](../adr/ADR-003-postgres-hosting.md)
- [docs/roadmap/17-security-privacy-and-abuse.md](17-security-privacy-and-abuse.md)

### Owned implementation surfaces

Planned targets unless present in the code tree:

```text
src/princess_app/domain/
src/princess_app/application/
src/princess_app/adapters/postgres/
src/princess_app/adapters/oidc/
apps/api/
migrations/
```

### Coding sequence

1. Implement initial principal/identity, asset/sample/capture, run/measurement/region, report, job/outbox and version tables with reviewed Alembic migrations; defer commerce-specific tables to T19.
2. Implement an append-only permission/consent event ledger and owner-scoped grant/withdraw lifecycle for service processing, retention, third-party AI processing, contribution, ordinary sharing and partner comparison as distinct purposes, using T03 purpose/policy IDs; check effective permission at use time rather than mutating historical grants.
3. Map verified provider identities to internal principals; implement guest-to-account transfer and deletion/session revocation. No home-grown password system or email-only account linking.
4. Persist canonical result JSON and relational projections atomically; enforce owner/run composite references and actual non-owner runtime roles.
5. Publish authenticated API composition and repository/unit-of-work fakes plus PostgreSQL integration fixtures.

### Contract and integration handoff

Stable internal ownership IDs, transaction boundaries and versioned persistence interfaces; no provider objects leak into DTOs.

### Acceptance evidence

- Cross-owner/run access and duplicate features are rejected by application and relevant database constraints.
- Actual PostgreSQL role/RLS and migration/restore smoke pass; reference members remain service-only.
- Permission grants/withdrawals persist as append-only purpose/policy/scope events; stale or withdrawn permission cannot authorize later processing.
- Partner-comparison authorization is a separate purpose from ordinary sharing, with independent grant/withdraw/audit state checked at use time.

### Required failure and regression cases

- Guessed report IDs, forged region parent, guest-transfer race, revoked token, duplicate projection write and migration rollback with existing rows.
- Permission replay, stale policy version, concurrent withdraw/use, contribution without authority and AI processing after withdrawal.
- Ordinary share grant reused as partner-comparison authority, withdrawn partner comparison reused by a stale invitation, and concurrent partner withdrawal/use.

### Deliverables

- Migrations, repositories/unit of work and identity adapter
- Owner-scoped API and non-owner role tests
- Permission-event schema/repository/service and grant/withdraw API lifecycle

### Rollback and compatibility

- Use expand/contract migrations and revoke provider bindings safely; never restore deleted ownership from a stale cache.

### Validation and human gates

Validation profiles: [core](#validation-core), [docs](#validation-docs), [contracts](#validation-contracts), [backend](#validation-backend), [connectors](#validation-connectors). Planned suites must be implemented and their actual command documented by the owning task; they are not passing tests today.

- `processor_retention_contracts`: Approved providers, regions, purposes, retention/deletion and support obligations.

No approval is created by this task brief. Mock/disabled implementation is not authorization for live collection, charges, signing or release.

### Coding sequence

1. Draft purpose-specific consent/withdrawal, retention and source-license contracts without inventing approvals; define partner comparison as a distinct purpose from ordinary sharing, and coordinate final DTO mapping with T01.
2. Prepare original Swedish/English controlled/free-writing prompts and capture/author guidance, keeping copied tasks separate from free writing and repeat captures separate from writers.
3. Specify deletion lineage, participant/source rights evidence, adult eligibility and unsupported context handling for owner review.
4. Provide fixtures for grant/deny/withdraw/no-authority cases and a gated pilot handoff; actual recruitment belongs to T11.

### Contract and integration handoff

Versioned purpose/protocol IDs and approved-or-pending evidence references; service permission, contribution, AI processing, ordinary sharing and partner comparison are distinct purposes.

### Acceptance evidence

- Declining contribution does not reduce Free; no prechecked sharing/donation.
- Source code, data and model-weight rights are distinguished; retention is a reviewed configuration, not a legal claim.

### Required failure and regression cases

- Payment mistaken for AI consent, uploader lacks author permission, withdrawal during use, reused obsolete notice, duplicate specimen counted as a writer.

### Deliverables

- Draft consent/retention/source-rights specifications
- Original collection prompts and protocol fixtures

### Rollback and compatibility

- Version notices/protocols; revoke future uses without silently changing the meaning of historical grants.

## T04 — Safe intake and durable analysis jobs

**Status:** `DONE` · **Owner:** backend · **Milestone:** free

**Hard predecessors:** [T02](#t02), [T03](#t03), [T28](#t28)
**Platforms:** backend, workers
**Connector ports:** ObjectStore, AbuseChallengeProvider

### Required reading

- [docs/roadmap/05-release-operations.md](05-release-operations.md)
- [docs/connectors/object-storage.md](../connectors/object-storage.md)
- [docs/connectors/abuse-challenge.md](../connectors/abuse-challenge.md)

### Owned implementation surfaces

Planned targets unless present in the code tree:

```text
apps/api/
apps/workers/analysis/
src/princess_app/application/intake/
src/princess_app/adapters/storage/
```

### Coding sequence

1. Implement owner/quota-bound upload reservation and completion, media sniffing, bounded decode/sanitization and tested mobile-format conversion policy.
2. Promote verified bytes to an immutable internal asset/version before scheduling; retain digest and coordinate-transform lineage.
3. Expose `POST /v1/analyses` as the explicit idempotent transition from a completed immutable sample/capture to one deterministic AnalysisRun/job; upload completion validates/promotes bytes but does not silently create a run.
4. Implement PostgreSQL job/outbox, short leases, attempt records and fenced publication outside long transactions. Add a heartbeat only if measured real latency approaches the lease budget.
5. Provide owner-scoped status/cancel/delete behavior and safe failure codes; restrict CPU/memory/provider egress and admission cost.

### Contract and integration handoff

An immutable authorized capture and durable AnalysisRun/job reference; source bytes and processed frame are never conflated.

### Acceptance evidence

- Repeated completion/submission converges on one intended result.
- Stale workers and delete-during-run cannot publish; Free is bounded and provider independent.

### Required failure and regression cases

- Pixel bomb, spoofed MIME, animated/malformed file, HEIC orientation, signed-URL overwrite race, checksum mismatch, expired upload, queue crash and stale lease.

### Deliverables

- Safe intake routes and storage adapter
- Durable analysis worker with limits/fencing
- Failure/format compatibility fixtures

### Rollback and compatibility

- Stop admission and drain/fence leases; preserve verified inputs only under retention and never republish tombstoned captures.

### Validation and human gates

Validation profiles: [core](#validation-core), [docs](#validation-docs), [backend](#validation-backend), [connectors](#validation-connectors). Planned suites must be implemented and their actual command documented by the owning task; they are not passing tests today.

- `processor_retention_contracts`: Approved providers, regions, purposes, retention/deletion and support obligations.

### Contract and integration handoff

### Implementation evidence

PR #14 established the working deterministic Free Next.js journey and T21 export integration. This T17 slice adds canonical ReportSummary/ReportPage contracts, owner-scoped paginated report history, report-scoped EvidenceBundle reads with stored digest/lineage validation, current-principal history UI, stored baseline/spacing/slant evidence views and cross-owner/browser regression coverage. PR #18 adds a reviewed pinned axe dependency and generated lockfile, automated WCAG A/AA browser-state coverage with a proven negative control, explicit fixture/live Playwright modes, and a mandatory isolated live Free upload-to-export CI journey that refreshes the queued run before deterministic worker execution. PR #33 promotes new analyses to individual-report/2 while preserving explicit legacy-v1 reports/revisions, applies the owner-accepted Inktrospect Dossier hierarchy to First Reveal/report/evidence/history, and adds browser/accessibility coverage for positive highlight, reviewed no-eligible fallback, narrow Swedish, 200% text and dark/reduced-motion states without introducing client-side salience. The production-identity review then found that the deterministic fake had been equating token issuance with authentication freshness even though the generic OIDC adapter deliberately leaves missing auth_time unknown. This credential-freshness repair separates those concepts, rejects impossible future auth_time before application state mutation and keeps the current ID-token-shaped OIDC profile narrow pending ADR-002. The provider-owned credential-policy slice then removes the remaining OIDC-specific audience assumption from the application boundary: IdentityService no longer receives an audience and VerifiedIdentity no longer carries one. The current fake/OIDC adapters retain their own configured audience checks, so provider-specific context policy can later differ without weakening application authorization. The next provider-specific slice code-qualifies a production-disabled Supabase Auth candidate against pinned supabase/auth source semantics: one first-party asymmetric access-JWT profile with configured audience/roles, canonical UUID subject/session, non-anonymous state and conservative timestamped-AMR freshness. Refresh-token issuance time is not promoted to authentication time; missing/unknown AMR remains unknown, and Custom Access Token Hooks/HS256 projects stay outside the qualified profile. API composition and environment manifests remain provider-free. The web credential-session hardening slice then reconciles the existing client architecture instead of adding a redundant backend session port: web already had a server-only HttpOnly-cookie credential source and native already had SecureSessionStore/NativeSessionBoundary. T17 centralizes web issue/clear cookie policy, renames the server reader to provider-neutral sessionCredential, proves no browser storage/provider parsing occurs in the transport, and keeps local-device clear, application logout-everywhere and provider revocation as distinct lifecycles. The managed-project qualification-tooling slice first added an explicit offline Supabase account-profile harness. The post-#46 hardening keeps synthetic CI offline but makes MANAGED_PROJECT evidence live and interlocked: the tool performs a real refresh with protected refresh material plus a low-privilege publishable/legacy-anon key, requires explicit anonymous/OAuth-server/hook inspection, then waits for an owner-performed asymmetric signing-key rotation and genuine new sign-in. A v2 receipt records token lifetime, JWKS key IDs/hashes, AMR methods and refresh/rotation/reauth/revocation-fence witnesses without storing token, refresh token, API key, subject, session ID, issuer URL or JWKS body. Tooling still does not constitute provider selection or an actual managed-project PASS. PR #48 then factors provider-facing JWKS retrieval into one fixed-issuer, redirect-refusing, byte/key-count-bounded `SupabaseJwksSource` reused by qualification; API/runtime identity composition remains fake-only, so this networking primitive does not cross the ADR-002 owner/account gate. The identity-provider decision-evidence slice adds a dated primary-source Supabase-vs-Clerk comparison covering PKCE/native Apple+Google, private relay, linking/recovery, session revocation/deletion, JWT/JWKS/freshness, residency, pricing/rate limits, test tooling and migration. It records Clerk's automatic verified-email OAuth linking and unqualified factor-age freshness as Princess-specific review blockers, while explicitly preserving Supabase as CANDIDATE and leaving managed-project/account/owner approval pending. The ADR-002 owner-selection slice records the 2026-10-01 product/technical-owner decision to use Supabase Auth as the implementation provider, bound to the dated Supabase-vs-Clerk evidence and the existing first-party access-JWT direction. It deliberately leaves the managed-project PASS, processor/account approval, runtime composition and production activation pending. The Supabase receipt-v3 hardening slice disables ambient HTTPX environment trust on the live refresh exchange, refuses redirects, bounds refresh-response bytes, redacts transport failures, and records whether managed evidence is QUALIFICATION_ONLY or INTENDED_RUNTIME_PROFILE. A Git-safe evidence index remains PENDING until a real owner-authorized run; the exact receipt stays protected. The environment-bound receipt-v4 slice records environment/provider mode plus the reviewed manifest hash and refuses qualification scopes that disagree with the environment manifests. Staging/sandbox and production/live therefore remain separate technical evidence gates. The 2026-10-01 managed-project run then passed receipt v4 against the owner-authorized intended staging identity profile (`project_alias=princess-staging`, `environment=staging`, `provider_mode=sandbox`, `project_binding=INTENDED_RUNTIME_PROFILE`) bound to Princess commit 033b9b9c32ee296a28431fbe85d87f3c7ab9199d and the reviewed staging manifest. The live witness proved a first-party password session, same-session provider refresh with unchanged AMR-derived authentication freshness, ES256/P-256 signing-key rotation retaining old and new asymmetric keys in JWKS, genuine new-session password reauthentication with newer freshness, and the Princess revoked_before fence rejecting the refreshed pre-reauth credential while accepting the post-rotation reauthentication. This closes only the staging/sandbox exact-profile technical gate; production/live, processor/account review and runtime composition remain pending. The scoped Supabase staging account/processor review slice then assembles the Git-safe account evidence required after #53: actual staging region/plan, the narrow `IdentityProvider`/`VERIFY_CREDENTIAL` test purpose, authentication data categories, DPA/region/deletion/rate-limit source references, least-privilege boundaries, unsupported lifecycle operations and re-review triggers. It deliberately leaves the human owner decision pending and does not modify consent/legal-basis records, runtime composition, environment manifests or the shared `processor_retention_contracts` gate. The post-#54 evidence-hardening slice repairs the late review findings without changing runtime code: it binds the staging region/plan to a Git-safe Management API snapshot with hashed provider identifiers; separates Princess's `VERIFY_CREDENTIAL` runtime capability from operator-controlled disposable test-user sign-in/session issuance/refresh used only to mint conformance credentials; documents DPA/subprocessor/support, cost and retry ownership; adds a provider-aware manual exit procedure that revokes sessions before deleting test users and keeps the Princess fence active while access JWTs age out; and moves exact selected-account Auth rate-limit/retry evidence into T17 acceptance rather than a prospective PR number. The human owner decision remains pending. The staging-composition slice records the explicit owner approval for the narrow verification scope, keeps the qualified staging manifest byte-identical, adds a protected receipt-to-runtime binding tool and central protected-config grant, composes Supabase only for `(staging, sandbox)`, keeps dev-token minting fake-only, and advances preflight's expected failure to the next unimplemented staging connector rather than faking the environment. The staging runtime-conformance tooling slice adds an explicit opt-in operator harness that consumes only an already-issued disposable staging access JWT plus the protected v4 receipt/issuer, rebuilds the qualified runtime binding, exercises the actual `compose_identity_provider` -> live bounded JWKS -> `SupabaseIdentityProvider` -> `IdentityService` path with an in-memory identity store, and can emit only a privacy-safe Git index while the operational receipt stays outside the checkout. The tool does not sign in, refresh, accept API/admin keys, use PostgreSQL or claim a real PASS until the owner-authorized live witness occurs. The Auth operational-policy tooling slice defines the second pre-login gate without activating login: a protected-input builder verifies the already-qualified staging project-ref hash, allowlists the selected account's Management API Auth rate-limit/forwarded-IP settings into a deterministic Git-safe snapshot, refuses missing/wrongly typed/default-substituted evidence, and keeps retry ownership application-side with no invented timing constants. The policy requires provider cooldown precedence, no automatic bad-credential retry and single-flight refresh, while leaving the actual selected-account snapshot PENDING until a real owner-authorized `/config/auth` export is captured. The staging Auth closeout-control slice adds a strict non-identifying cleanup-evidence builder plus an atomic closeout checker. The checker requires the real runtime conformance PASS, real selected-account Auth-settings snapshot and real disposable-provider cleanup evidence together, validates that all evidence remains bound to the qualified staging project, and refuses to pass if the existing owner record is widened into application-login, production or global-gate approval. The closeout document also fixes the clean-worktree sequencing trap: conformance must run from a clean checkout before Git-safe snapshot generation dirties a worktree. The post-#59 evidence-chain hardening pins closeout to the frozen post-#58 conformance commit, parses and validates the complete Git-safe conformance record rather than a handful of PASS lines, and versions cleanup evidence as `supabase-staging-cleanup/2` with the exact runtime conformance receipt SHA. This prevents cleanup from another disposable witness or a hand-shaped PASS document from satisfying the atomic closeout checker. PR #63 then aligns the operator runbook with the exact cleanup-v2 input contract, registers that runbook in the T17 machine graph, and rejects cleanup evidence dated before its bound conformance receipt. The pre-live #64 hardening advances Auth-settings evidence to `supabase-auth-settings/2`, derives a SHA-256 over the exact protected `/config/auth` response bytes with an opaque protected-evidence reference, and makes the final atomic checker independently enforce `conformance <= Auth-settings <= cleanup` chronology. The pre-live line-ending repair proves the 2026-10-01 protected v4 receipt was generated from the unchanged staging manifest on a clean Windows CRLF checkout; new qualification hashes normalize line endings, the exact historical receipt/CRLF anchor remains pinned, and runtime drift is bound to the LF-normalized Git manifest. Corrected runtime witness freeze: `c653a7d0cc29e0398a0cfb9e5c8113b9b2acd6b3`.

### Remaining work

- Operationally close the staging Auth evidence gates against frozen conformance baseline `c653a7d0cc29e0398a0cfb9e5c8113b9b2acd6b3`: from a clean worktree run the owner-authorized real Supabase staging conformance and retain its protected receipt/Git-safe PASS whose complete evidence record validates against that exact commit and all qualified anchors; from a separate clean worktree capture the selected staging project's real `GET /v1/projects/{ref}/config/auth` response and generate `docs/ci/T17_SUPABASE_AUTH_SETTINGS_SNAPSHOT.json`; then revoke all sessions for the same disposable conformance test user, delete that disposable Auth user, generate `docs/ci/T17_SUPABASE_STAGING_CLEANUP_EVIDENCE.json` using cleanup schema v2 with the exact conformance receipt SHA, and require `python tools/check_supabase_staging_auth_closeout.py --auth-config-file /protected/princess-staging-auth-config.json` to PASS. Tooling/synthetic tests do not close these gates. After the three evidence classes close, application-managed web authentication/session implementation may proceed under a separate disabled/reviewed scope; the 2026-10-01 decision still does not approve application-login activation. Provider lifecycle integration, recovery/linking, Apple/Google/private-relay behavior and production/live qualification remain later work.

### Acceptance evidence

- Refresh/reconnect resumes the known job rather than creating work; provider-disabled Free works.
- No server keys or paid hidden data in client payloads; supported browser/accessibility journeys pass.
- Logout/deletion freshness is fail-closed: newly issued credentials without proven post-revocation authentication cannot restore access or rebind a deleted identity.
- IdentityService consumes only already-verified provider identity facts; audience/authorized-party/token-context rules are enforced by the selected adapter and cannot be bypassed by application callers.
- Selected Supabase profile refresh cannot cross the durable revoked_before fence unless signed timestamped AMR proves a reviewed authentication/reauthentication ceremony after the fence.
- Web credential transport is opaque and server-only: issue/clear cookies share one reviewed HttpOnly/SameSite/path/Secure policy, and the proxy forwards the credential without provider parsing.
- An owner-authorized Supabase qualification project can be qualified without committing credential material: the harness performs a live same-session refresh, witnesses unchanged auth_time, requires a live asymmetric signing-key rotation plus genuine new-session reauthentication, and records token/JWKS/profile/fence facts in a privacy-safe receipt.
- Identity-provider decision evidence distinguishes public documentation, Princess-specific qualification, account/processor approval and production activation; none may substitute for another.
- Managed Supabase evidence states whether it binds only a qualification project or the intended runtime profile; qualification-only evidence cannot silently close the exact runtime-profile gate.
- Supabase managed-project evidence is environment-scoped: staging/sandbox qualification cannot be presented as production/live qualification, and the receipt binds the reviewed environment manifest hash.
- Supabase staging account/processor evidence records the actual provider scope, region/plan, data categories and unresolved retention/support/subprocessor facts separately from the human owner decision; public documentation or account metadata cannot manufacture approval.
- Supabase staging region/plan assertions are bound to a dated Git-safe Management API snapshot with hashed provider identifiers; account facts without source-bound evidence cannot satisfy the staging account review.
- Before any application-managed Supabase sign-in or refresh flow is activated, T17 records the exact relevant selected-account Auth endpoint limits, retry/backoff ownership and abuse-control policy; a prospective PR number is never the gate.
- The staging identity exit path has provider-owner cleanup evidence: global session/refresh revocation, Princess revoked_before fencing while access JWTs age out, disposable Auth-user deletion, and separately authorized project decommission evidence when the whole project is retired.
- Staging identity composition accepts only the qualified `(staging, sandbox)` Supabase profile when protected runtime values match the receipt-derived binding anchored to the recorded v4 receipt, account snapshot and qualified manifest; test/preview/staging-live/production remain fail-closed.
- A real Supabase staging runtime conformance PASS may be recorded only when one already-issued disposable staging credential traverses the actual `compose_identity_provider` -> `SupabaseJwksSource` -> `SupabaseIdentityProvider` -> `IdentityService` path with the qualified binding; protected inputs/full receipt stay outside Git and the safe index contains no provider subject/session, Princess principal ID, raw issuer/project reference or credential material.
- Selected-account Supabase Auth operational evidence is source-bound to the already-qualified staging project: a real `GET /v1/projects/{ref}/config/auth` export is allowlisted into a Git-safe snapshot with the exact relevant rate-limit values and `security_sb_forwarded_for_enabled`; public defaults, missing fields or another project cannot satisfy the gate.
- Application-managed Auth retry ownership is explicit before activation: bad credentials/permanent failures are not automatically retried, provider rate-limit cooldowns take precedence, transient retries remain bounded/application-owned, and refresh is single-flight per session. No evidence-only PR invents transport retry constants before the transport exists.
- Staging Auth closeout is atomic across evidence classes: runtime conformance PASS, selected-account Auth-settings snapshot and disposable-provider cleanup evidence must all validate against the same qualified staging project before the closeout checker passes; one or two classes cannot close the gate.
- Staging cleanup evidence records all sessions for the disposable conformance test user revoked and that user's Auth account deleted without provider user/session identifiers, while preserving application_login inactive, project_decommission NOT_APPLICABLE, JWT age-out required and production disabled.
- Runtime-conformance closeout evidence is bound to the corrected frozen runtime-witness commit `c653a7d0cc29e0398a0cfb9e5c8113b9b2acd6b3` and the complete Git-safe conformance record validates receipt version/digest plus the recorded qualification, account, manifest, project, issuer, audience, role and source-revision anchors.
- Disposable-provider cleanup evidence uses `supabase-staging-cleanup/2` and carries the exact runtime `conformance_receipt_sha256`; cleanup for another witness cannot be combined with the selected-account snapshot to close T17.
- Disposable-provider cleanup evidence cannot predate the bound runtime-conformance witness; its checked_date must be the same as or later than the protected conformance receipt checked_date.
- Selected-account Auth-settings evidence uses `supabase-auth-settings/3`, binds the allowlisted safe projection to the SHA-256 of the exact protected Management API `/config/auth` response bytes plus an opaque protected-evidence reference, and carries canonical `evidence_sha256` over the complete Git-safe snapshot envelope. Final closeout must re-read the exact protected raw Auth-config response and require its SHA-256 plus every allowlisted value to match the Git-safe snapshot; recomputing the public envelope hash is not provider provenance.
- Final staging Auth closeout independently enforces chronology across evidence classes: runtime conformance checked_date <= Auth-settings captured_date <= cleanup checked_date.
- Supabase qualification manifest hashing is line-ending stable: the exact historical Windows CRLF v4 receipt remains receipt-SHA-pinned while runtime drift detection uses the LF-normalized/Git manifest hash.

### Required failure and regression cases

- Auth expiry, late prior-account response, cross-owner URL, revoked report, corrupt payload, upload failure, long labels and zero/missing charts.
- Fresh token issuance without auth_time after logout/deletion, stale auth_time, future auth_time, and assuming a configured session secret or provider sid means provider revocation occurred.
- Application-supplied audience overriding adapter policy, wrong-audience OIDC/fake credential accepted after the refactor, and treating a VerifiedIdentity audience field as downstream authorization.
- Supabase HS256/shared-secret project, multi/foreign audience, service/admin role, anonymous session, OAuth-server client_id profile, missing/malformed session UUID, malformed/future AMR and unaudited Custom Access Token Hook.
- Web credential stored in localStorage/sessionStorage, provider/JWT parsing added to the Next transport, invalid web environment silently treated as production/local, cookie-clear attributes drifting from issuance, or local-device sign-out claimed as provider/session revocation.
- Qualification run without explicit opt-in, secret/service-role key supplied, raw token/refresh/API-key/subject/session/issuer/JWKS leaked into the receipt, enabled/unknown Custom Access Token Hook accepted, anonymous/OAuth-server account settings left unknown, refresh changes session/auth_time, signing kid fails to rotate, reauthentication fails to create a newer session/freshness, or synthetic fixture presented as managed-project evidence.
- Public vendor documentation treated as owner/provider approval, Supabase implementation maturity treated as automatic selection, Clerk verified-email linking treated as Princess merge proof, or MAU and MRU pricing compared as identical units.
- Ambient HTTP proxy/CA configuration influencing the live refresh exchange, oversized/redirected refresh responses, a synthetic or qualification-only receipt presented as exact runtime-profile evidence, or a raw managed-project receipt committed to Git.
- Staging/sandbox receipt relabelled as production/live evidence, qualification environment/provider mode disagreeing with the reviewed manifest, or a receipt validated against a different environment-manifest hash.
- Supabase public DPA/security pages or observed account region/plan treated as automatic processor approval, staging `VERIFY_CREDENTIAL` approval broadened to public login/OAuth/handwriting/Storage/analytics, or the scoped decision used to mark the shared `processor_retention_contracts` gate globally complete.
- Staging approval scoped only to VERIFY_CREDENTIAL while silently relying on unapproved provider sign-in/session issuance/refresh, region/plan asserted without a source-bound account snapshot, rollback that disables Princess but leaves provider sessions/users active, or Auth rate-limit obligations deferred only to a future PR number.
- Receipt-derived binding with wrong receipt/account/manifest/project/issuer/audience/role, protected identity profile inputs outside the staging API, or making full staging green by substituting fake ObjectStore/Payment/Abuse providers.
- Staging conformance tool performing sign-in/refresh, accepting API/admin keys, writing protected material inside the checkout, bypassing `compose_identity_provider`, requiring PostgreSQL/full API startup to prove identity, leaking token/issuer/subject/session/principal data, or presenting synthetic/tooling evidence as a live provider PASS.
- Auth-settings evidence captured from the wrong project, copied from public defaults, missing required selected-account values, containing raw project/provider secrets, accepting bool/string/negative rate limits, widening unknown provider fields into Git, or using the evidence snapshot to activate application login/production.
- Authentication retry policy with hidden SDK retries, automatic bad-credential retry, tight-loop 429 handling, parallel refresh fan-out, arbitrary client-supplied forwarded IP trust, or fixed retry timing invented before the actual login/session transport is reviewed.
- Closeout claimed from a dirty/synthetic conformance run, selected-account snapshot generated before the clean conformance witness in the same worktree, cleanup claimed by editing the conformance receipt, revoking unrelated project users/sessions, project decommission falsely claimed, or any two-of-three evidence subset presented as complete.
- Staging closeout checker that rewrites the 2026-10-01 narrow owner decision into application-login/production approval or permits the closeout while application_login owner authority is widened.
- PASS-shaped conformance Markdown from the wrong Princess commit, missing/forged receipt digest, altered qualification/account/manifest/profile anchor, or cleanup evidence whose conformance_receipt_sha256 differs from the runtime witness.
- Cleanup evidence with checked_date earlier than its bound runtime-conformance receipt, even when all cleanup booleans and receipt digest otherwise validate.
- Auth-settings snapshot with an edited/invalid source_response_sha256, a recomputed v3 envelope that is not backed by the exact protected raw `/config/auth` bytes at final closeout, invalid protected evidence reference, or source bytes whose allowlisted values differ from the committed snapshot.
- Final closeout using Auth-settings captured before runtime conformance or cleanup dated before either the runtime witness or Auth-settings capture.
- LF/CRLF checkout differences for the unchanged staging manifest must not force requalification or weaken exact receipt pinning; actual normalized manifest content drift must still fail closed.

### Deliverables

- Web client and browser/accessibility contract tests
- Production-disabled selected Supabase Auth profile verifier and synthetic qualification fixtures
- Web credential-session policy and transport regression tests
- Offline Supabase managed-project qualification harness and privacy-safe receipt contract
- Dated ADR-002 Supabase-vs-Clerk provider decision evidence with explicit unknown/account gates
- Git-safe Supabase managed-project evidence index with protected receipt digest/reference and explicit project binding
- Scoped Supabase staging account/processor evidence record with explicit staging-only owner approval and production/global-gate non-claims
- Git-safe Supabase staging account-settings snapshot binding region/plan to provider Management API evidence
- Protected Supabase staging runtime-binding tool plus exact-tuple composition/preflight regression coverage
- Operator-only Supabase staging runtime conformance harness with protected receipt and Git-safe evidence index
- Supabase Auth operational-policy contract plus source-bound selected-account settings snapshot builder
- Supabase staging Auth closeout contract, cleanup-evidence builder and atomic closeout checker
- Source-bound Supabase Auth-settings v3 evidence-envelope contract plus final cross-artifact chronology validation.

### Rollback and compatibility

- Deploy compatible presentation versions and clear unsafe caches; preserve API compatibility and saved reports.

### Validation and human gates

Validation profiles: [docs](#validation-docs), [contracts](#validation-contracts), [js_packages](#validation-js_packages), [web_browser](#validation-web_browser), [web_render](#validation-web_render), [backend](#validation-backend). ## T19 — Cross-platform purchase ledger entitlements and metered jobs

**Status:** `IN_PROGRESS` · **Owner:** commerce · **Milestone:** premium

**Hard predecessors:** [T02](#t02), [T03](#t03), [T09](#t09), [T15](#t15), [T27](#t27)
**Platforms:** backend, workers
**Connector ports:** PaymentProvider

### Required reading

- [docs/roadmap/14-payments-entitlements-and-commerce.md](14-payments-entitlements-and-commerce.md)
- [docs/connectors/payments.md](../connectors/payments.md)

- [docs/roadmap/13-android-and-google-play.md](13-android-and-google-play.md)
- [docs/adr/ADR-006-payments.md](../adr/ADR-006-payments.md)

### Owned implementation surfaces

Planned targets unless present in the code tree:

```text
src/princess_app/domain/commerce/
src/princess_app/application/commerce/
src/princess_app/adapters/stripe/
src/princess_app/adapters/apple/
src/princess_app/adapters/google/
apps/api/
migrations/
```

### Coding sequence

1. Create internal catalog/provider mappings, verified event inbox, unique financial transactions, immutable credit lots/ledger, reservation and fulfilment states.
2. Qualify production-disabled Stripe hosted checkout/webhooks/authoritative lookup/reconcile, then implement Apple signed/server-notification verification and Play token/RTDN verification with environment/account binding.
3. Grant a durable credit atomically then promptly finish/consume/acknowledge via the product-appropriate provider path; never wait for AI completion.
4. Reserve one eligible credit per intended Premium job; fence publication, release/compensate failure and reconcile ambiguous provider outcomes.
5. Implement repeated restore, refunds/voided events, account deletion and cross-platform origin-policy enforcement; backend work does not depend on native UI completion.

### Contract and integration handoff

Server-owned catalog, purchase claims/status, credit/fulfilment APIs and reconciliation workers for web/iOS/Android.

### Implementation evidence

PR #14 commit 6d7fc25 plus review repairs implemented the server-owned catalog draft, verified event inbox, immutable financial ledger, origin-rail credit lots, reservations, metered Premium publication/spend and reconciliation semantics using fake rails. PR #35 adds a production-disabled StripePaymentProvider using the reviewed backend httpx lock: server-catalog hosted Checkout with provider idempotency, raw-body Stripe-Signature verification, relevant-event normalization, authoritative PaymentIntent lookup, bounded reconciliation, account/product/environment/refund-state mapping and typed/redacted failures. In-process transport tests plus a PostgreSQL CommerceService integration prove redirect-without-grant and duplicate signed-event convergence to one ledger grant; application composition remains explicitly fake-only. PR #36 completes the provider-side implementation slice: Stripe full-refund requests are exposed only under a separate explicit refund approval; Apple validates ES256/x5c signed StoreKit transaction material, Notifications V2, appAccountToken/bundle/environment/product binding, Get Transaction Info and bounded Notification History backfill; Google validates ProductPurchaseV2, package/product/obfuscated-account binding, authenticated Pub/Sub RTDN, post-grant consume/acknowledge and bounded Voided Purchases backfill. Deterministic adapter tests plus PostgreSQL CommerceService integration prove Apple duplicate signed transactions grant once with client finish and Google duplicate purchase-token claims grant once with server consume. Application composition remains fake-only.

### Remaining work

- Exercise the implemented Stripe adapter against an approved Stripe sandbox/account and retain checkout/webhook/authoritative-lookup/reconcile/refund evidence under the approved product/refund policy.
- Exercise the implemented App Store adapter with approved Apple sandbox/TestFlight transactions and Notifications V2, including account binding, refund/revocation, Notification History backfill and post-grant client finish evidence.
- Exercise the implemented Google Play adapter with approved license-test/internal-track purchases and authenticated RTDN, including pending-to-purchased, consume/acknowledge, voided-purchase backfill and replay evidence.
- Resolve approved products/prices/tax/refund/storefront/credit-portability policy, including the owner decision for refund-after-spend Premium access, and approve provider regions/retention/support obligations before any non-fake composition.

### Acceptance evidence

- Only verified PURCHASED/paid states grant, once per financial identity; client redirects/flags never grant.
- Concurrency and crash tests prove no double spend/grant and no lost durable credit; refunds are compensating events.

### Required failure and regression cases

- Pending payment, wrong product/account/environment, duplicate/reordered events, grant-before-finish crash, consume timeout, last-credit race, refund after spend and replay after deletion.

### Deliverables

- Ledger/migrations, three backend payment adapters, sandbox evidence and reconciliation runbook

### Rollback and compatibility

- Disable new sales/fulfilment safely while preserving audit and reconciliation; never delete financial history or remint restored transactions.

- `processor_retention_contracts`: Approved providers, regions, purposes, retention/deletion and support obligations.

### Coding sequence

1. Deploy staging and approved production topology with narrow worker roles, migrations, private storage, secret rotation and independent capability kill switches.
2. Implement outbox mail/APNs/FCM delivery and safe telemetry/analytics adapters with failure isolation, token/suppression lifecycle and named alert owners.
3. Implement the authenticated report-feedback API, minimal/redacted persistence, retention/deletion lifecycle and restricted support-review access; feedback is not a telemetry event and may not include raw handwriting or unrestricted report payloads.
4. Exercise backups/restore with deletion tombstones, durable job/payment reconciliation, model outage, cost limits and compatible mobile/API rollout.
5. Write actionable incident/refund/deletion/key compromise/store halt and version rollback runbooks with actual deployed commands and support responsibility.

### Contract and integration handoff

Operable staged infrastructure and recovery/notification/support evidence, not public release approval.

### Implementation evidence

PR #14 slices 19b00a0, 3b2087e, 5a22ba4 and final repair d2e1063 implemented redacted report feedback, ops commands/runbooks, append-only restore tombstones for deletions/withdrawals/logout-everywhere, and an outbox-driven notification state machine with kill switch and fake mail/push adapters. This repair adds transactionally queued outbox events plus external restore tombstones for single-device logout and feedback withdrawal, with temporal replay guards that preserve newer re-registration/resubmission. PR #20 exposes the existing account report-ready mail preference through the typed client and exact same-origin web proxy, with guest refusal, persistence, CSRF/route-boundary and accessibility coverage in the isolated live-web journey; no mail provider is activated. PR #21 adds deterministic restore-stable Premium attempt IDs, a sanitized durable provider-attempt journal, fake-qualified authoritative attempt lookup, and an explicit fail-closed restored-Premium reconciliation pass that prevents automatic second generation after backup restore; the current OpenAI store=false adapter remains lookup-unsupported and live activation stays gated. The T24 runtime-topology slice adds reviewed linux/amd64 source-tree backend/export images, a fixed role dispatcher, provider-free startup preflight, DB-only API/worker readiness, zero-authority dormant render/reference manifest grants, a separate non-owner smoke-role bootstrap and synthetic Docker Compose qualification; it does not select or activate production hosting/providers. The provider-neutral recovery rehearsal adds a destructive-test-fenced real PostgreSQL custom-format pg_dump/pg_restore cycle with synthetic private state: it leaves object/tombstone storage forward in time, proves the restored database genuinely resurrects a deleted capture/account/permission grant, reuses the existing tombstone replay and erasure paths to remove them again, rejects a corrupted backup and emits a privacy-safe recovery-receipt/1 with observed timings rather than invented RPO/RTO claims. The operational-posture slice adds migration 0011 with a fixed SECURITY DEFINER aggregate function, operational-snapshot/1, a strict exporter-neutral alert-policy contract, provider-independent snapshot/check/verify-disabled operator commands and final-runtime CI proving both PASS and stale-queue ALERT paths. The normal runtime role remains RLS-scoped for raw rows; no dynamic control plane, production threshold, dashboard vendor or SLO is introduced. The release/rollback qualification slice adds environment-neutral runtime-release/1 manifests, method+route and two-way report compatibility gates, a separate candidate-migration/runtime-under-test Compose topology, cross-runtime Free report write/read smoke and the pinned real #38 0010→0011 expansion witness. Application rollback is explicitly forward-database-only and candidate-only queued work is required to be drained or fenced; no client-build minimum, registry digest, production provider or database downgrade is invented. The operational-telemetry mapping slice converts the fixed operational-snapshot/1 dimension universe and reviewed alerts into bounded TelemetryRecord gauges through BufferedTelemetry, zero-fills absent count dimensions to avoid stale series, and qualifies the fake exporter path in the final backend image without widening generic telemetry attributes or selecting a vendor.

### Remaining work

- Qualify and activate authoritative restored-Premium attempt lookup (or an equivalent reviewed idempotency mechanism) for the selected live model configuration before live Premium enablement; provider-neutral deterministic attempt journaling and fake-qualified fail-closed restore reconciliation are implemented.
- Select and qualify the production PostgreSQL plus object/tombstone providers, approve RPO/RTO from their actual backup/PITR/version-deletion capabilities, bind the qualified recovery choreography to them and retain a provider-backed timed restore/PITR drill.
- Implement live transactional mail plus signed bounce/complaint handling; integrate APNs/FCM with T29–T31 once native signing/accounts exist.
- Implement broader key rotation/compromise handling, account/identity recovery and store-rollout halt procedures.
- The provider-neutral operational-snapshot/1 → TelemetryExporter mapping is implemented; select and qualify the actual telemetry/dashboard and production host/registry/network/secret-manager stack, approve real staging/production thresholds, retention/routing and named escalation owners from deployed evidence, add hosting-edge/global rate limits, and retain provider-backed alert-route plus staged rollout/halt exercises.
- Add a lease heartbeat only if measured production latency makes the current lease unsafe.

### Acceptance evidence

- A restore cannot resurrect erased data or duplicate credits/provider calls.
- Provider outage preserves Free and safe business state; no private writing in dashboards or crash logs.
- Report feedback is owner/report-bound, redacted to an allowlisted contract, removable under the approved lifecycle and inaccessible to generic analytics/telemetry roles.
- Application rollback keeps the database forward and the immediately previous API/Free-analysis runtime can read and write against the candidate schema after queues are drained or fenced.
- Operational posture exports a complete bounded count-gauge snapshot through TelemetryExporter without direct SQL/vendor coupling, and telemetry failure cannot become business-state or readiness authority.

### Required failure and regression cases

- Mail/push outage, queue restoration, stale token, budget breaker, key revocation, expired DB connection, refund reconciliation and rollback to withdrawn benchmark.
- Feedback containing raw writing/full report payload, cross-owner report feedback, support-role overreach, duplicate submission, and deletion followed by backup/queue resurrection.
- Removed public method+route, incompatible product-contract major, one-way report-template change, candidate write unreadable by rollback runtime and historical additive-schema incompatibility.
- Sparse operational export leaving stale non-zero gauges, private/dynamic telemetry labels, sandbox/live silently falling back to fake telemetry, and exporter failure propagating into business state.

### Deliverables

- Deployment manifests, notification adapters, dashboards and tested runbooks
- Provider-neutral runtime release manifests and rollout-qualification receipts
- Provider-neutral operational snapshot-to-telemetry mapping and final-image fake-export qualification

### Rollback and compatibility

- Promote only tested compatible artifacts; preserve tombstones and immutable ledger while halting affected capabilities.

### Validation and human gates

Validation profiles: [docs](#validation-docs), [backend](#validation-backend), [connectors](#validation-connectors), [release](#validation-release). Planned suites must be implemented and their actual command documented by the owning task; they are not passing tests today.

- `processor_retention_contracts`: Approved providers, regions, purposes, retention/deletion and support obligations.

```text

packages/api-client/

tools/run_mobile_journey.sh
tools/build_android_handoff.sh
tools/run_android_handoff_journey.sh

```

### Coding sequence

1. Compose the native app from validated build-variant config: secure session manager, guarded API client with per-request credentials, journal, resumable capture workflow and foreground runner; keep fixture identity out of release builds.
2. Implement capture review/bounds, the journaled upload-to-report workflow with lost-response and process-death recovery, and the native Dossier/evidence/history/settings/feedback/export/comparison screens from saved authorized projections.
3. Implement provider-independent commerce orchestration (grant-before-finish, pending/unknown outcomes, account-before-purchase), Premium state/permission/overlay display, push registration and verified-link resolution behind the existing ports and fakes.
4. Add only the native-facing API contracts the slice consumes (run discovery, report-scoped deletion and source image, notice delivery, same-owner comparisons) with owner-scope tests, and drive the real composition against the development API and workers.

### Contract and integration handoff

Shared native client capabilities proven against fakes and the development API, consumed by T30 (Apple) and T31 (Android) platform qualification; not a signed binary, store transaction, device or release evidence.

### Implementation evidence

Implemented on branch claude/determined-volta-42hu9a from main d6b37beb5fbb4365b48ac6d1fa50e7051191f350 (mobile completion plan N01-N06, N08, N11, N12, N15, N16 client work and S01 contracts). Local executed evidence on that branch: tests_app (including new tests_app/test_native_api.py) 478 passed and tests 1169 passed on PostgreSQL 16; pnpm typecheck clean; api-client 17, report-core 11, mobile 67, web 23 and render 9 tests passed (render with the preinstalled Chromium); Android CNG prebuild and Metro exports compiled the whole app to Hermes bytecode for Android and iOS with no fake in the bundle; tools/run_mobile_journey.sh passed against the local API, analysis worker and export worker (guest session, server notice, lost completion response, process-death resume of the same run, Dossier model, evidence lineage, byte-identical retained source image, history, same-owner comparison, feedback, bearer PDF export, guest-to-account transfer, report and account deletion). Exact-head CI evidence is not recorded here until a pull request runs the workflows. Post-merge documentation reconciliation: PR #72 final head 2a119ba55a185f4ba66f0a7df0e3e30de085ec48 passed Roadmap 37155767212, CI 37155767215, Release compatibility 37155767231, Application environments 37155767234, Runtime topology 37155767236 and Native foundation 37155767217. These are retained PR-triggered results, not new executions on the merge SHA. Codex code/security review was quota-blocked, not approved. No native UI, physical-device, signed-build or store evidence is inferred. See docs/handover/current-state.md. Standalone Android developer handoff (reconciled from main 13ca478eca256c04ec2b22ee2ac91841dc8d0109 after PR #75 Dossier v3 and PR #76 retained v3 UX artifact): the existing development variant is built with :app:assembleRelease into a non-debuggable APK signed by the generated CNG debug key, embedding the Hermes application bundle and the development/local runtime configuration (http://127.0.0.1:8000 through adb reverse; Android cleartext only for the development variant via expo-build-properties); tools/verify_android_handoff.py fails closed without an embedded bundle or with staging/store/production identity, and apkanalyzer/apksigner check debuggable=false, SDK levels, launcher, forbidden permissions and debug signing. Maestro CLI 2.11.0 (checksum-pinned, no cloud) is the selected app-driving runner: the exact APK is installed on an explicitly provisioned API-36 x86_64 Google APIs emulator and drives the real Free journey through the Android system Photo Picker, the server notice's service-processing switch, a server-backed queued run with the analysis worker gated, force-stop and relaunch with app data kept, recovery of the same journaled operation, and completion into the saved Dossier/evidence screen; exact database counts prove one capture, one run, one report and one revision bound to the same run. The qualifying evidence is the exact-head Native foundation android-handoff job of the introducing pull request and, after merge, the main-push run whose BUILDINFO.json names its own source commit; no run ID is recorded here. One emulator is not physical-device, signing, store or T31 evidence.

### Remaining work

- Qualify the client on physical iPhone/iPad and Android phone/tablet development builds after native_signing_accounts: camera/HEIC/EXIF, crop, process death, secure-store reinstall, large text, VoiceOver/TalkBack, tablet layouts and link cold/warm start (T30/T31).
- Native provider sign-in/refresh/recovery (N07) waits for the T17 selected-account Auth settings and retry-policy closeout; only development identity and guest transfer exist.
- Qualify StoreKit and Play purchase proofs, pending/Ask to Buy and finish/consume recovery in real sandboxes after price_account_terms_before_charges (T19/T30/T31); the expo-iap adapter is unexercised.
- Persist comparisons and add invitations, partner grants and pair Premium (N13/N14) only after T22 authorization contracts; current comparisons are same-owner and unsaved.
- Deliver APNs/FCM pushes through an approved push provider with the kind/object_ref payload the client expects, after processor_retention_contracts (T24).

### Acceptance evidence

- A clean install reaches an explicit session state; a synthetic specimen traverses the real development API and analysis worker to a saved report rendered from the authorized projection; relaunch resumes the same run; no development credential path exists in staging/store configuration.
- Lost responses and process death at every workflow transition create no second capture, grant or run; client purchase states never grant credit; store transactions finish only after a durable server grant.

### Required failure and regression cases

- Lost reservation/PUT/completion/permission/start responses, expired slot, changed or missing local bytes, quota/capacity back-off, withdrawn permission, expired session, account switch during purchase, pending/unknown store outcome, malformed links, React Native URL approximation, denied push and unavailable camera.

### Deliverables

- Native composition, controllers, adapters and screens; native-facing API routes; live development-API journey tooling and evidence

### Rollback and compatibility

- Revert the client slice or disable affected capabilities by configuration; the added API routes are additive and owner-scoped, and the backend stays compatible with earlier clients.

Validation profiles: [docs](#validation-docs), [contracts](#validation-contracts), [native](#validation-native), [native-journey](#validation-native-journey), [native-android-handoff](#validation-native-android-handoff), [connectors](#validation-connectors).
